## 5. Comparisons per concurrency

Comparisons are made only within one concurrency and only between the two modes. Per repetition the
values of both modes are shown side by side with the run index (`#n`) and the position inside the ABBA
pair (`1st` or `2nd`), so that order and drift effects stay visible. Per mode the table gives the number
of repetitions, the median and the minimum to maximum range of the per-run values. The median of per-run
percentiles is not a percentile of the pooled data; no pooled percentile is computed. Only `usable` and
`caution` runs enter; `*` marks a `caution` run.

The sentence under each table comes from a closed set of templates. The rule, applied to the exact
values before rounding: (1) fewer than two repetitions in one mode: no comparison is stated; (2) equal
medians; (3) the ranges overlap (touching counts as overlap): the set cannot separate the modes;
(4) the difference of the medians is not larger than the largest within-mode range: the set cannot
separate the modes; (5) otherwise the mode with the higher median is named. The difference and the range
are descriptive only: a handful of repetitions per cell gives no stable estimate of the run-to-run
variation, so nothing is inferred and no test is applied.

In the tables and sentences of this section the values of a cell have as many decimals as are needed to keep
the facts the rule used visible; the fixed decimals stated in the section "Metric definitions and caveats"
apply everywhere else. The rule itself always uses the exact values.

Charts (one point per run, excluded runs are not drawn):

- [completed streams per second](benchmark/chart-completed-per-second.svg)
- [time to first chunk p50](benchmark/chart-ttfc-p50.svg)
- [time to first chunk p99](benchmark/chart-ttfc-p99.svg)
- [total stream duration p99](benchmark/chart-total-p99.svg)

Mode order of the plan: `shared`, `per-request`.

## 6. Gateway and simulator deltas

Counter deltas are the value after the measured phase minus the value before it, read from the same JVM
(each run starts fresh JVMs, so counters start at zero). Gauges are shown as the value before and after,
not as a delta. A counter that decreased is shown as it is and flagged by `CHECK_COUNTER_DECREASED`.
The snapshot before the phase is taken after the warm-up, so a delta covers the measured phase and the
short idle waits around it.

## 8. Metric definitions and caveats

- **Unit of analysis.** One measured run: one mode, one concurrency, one repetition. The warm-up phase of
  a run is listed in the inventory and not analysed.
- **Outcome counts and shares.** Request lines of `measured.jsonl` are counted by their `outcome`; the
  share is the count divided by the number of request lines of that run.
- **Completed streams per second.** The number of COMPLETED records whose outcome instant
  (`startOffsetNanos + totalNanos`) lies in the window `[rampUp, duration)` of the measured phase, divided
  by the window length in seconds. The window comes from the JSONL header and is compared with the
  manifest plan. The footer `elapsedNanos` is shown separately for context. Caveat: the model is closed
  (a fixed number of workers, each opening the next stream when the previous one ended) and the stream
  length is fixed, so this rate is largely determined by the concurrency, the stream length and the
  gateway limit; it is not a capacity measurement. When responses take longer, the offered load drops,
  because coordinated omission is not corrected.
- **Time to first byte (ttfb).** From the request start until the HTTP client delivered the complete
  response header block. It is not the arrival of the first body byte.
- **Time to first chunk (ttfc) and total.** ttfc runs until the buffer that completed the first `chunk`
  event arrived; the resolution is therefore that of buffer arrival, not of the single chunk. total runs
  until the outcome was decided. Only COMPLETED requests enter these distributions (the population of the
  load generator's own summary); a record without a value is not counted in the distribution and is shown
  as `missing`.
- **Percentiles.** Exact nearest rank: for the sorted values `x[1..n]`, the percentile `p` is
  `x[ceil(p/100 * n)]` and the maximum is `x[n]`. Ties need no special handling. With `n = 0` the value is
  `n/a`.
- **Inter-chunk gaps.** The percentiles are read from the HdrHistogram in the footer of the JSONL (three
  digits of precision, so about 0.1 % resolution, bucket-equivalent values). The population is every gap
  between consecutive chunks in every stream of the run, including streams that did not complete. When the
  histogram cannot be decoded or its count differs from `interChunkCount`, the values are `n/a`.
- **Generator delay.** `startOffsetNanos - scheduledOffsetNanos` of every request line: the delay of the
  load generator itself. It is a data quality indicator, not a measurement of the system under test.
- **Reject pause.** After an HTTP 503 a worker pauses before it sends the next request. In a run with many
  REJECTED requests the offered load therefore contains think time; the rates of such runs are not
  comparable with runs without rejections.
- **Same machine.** The load generator, the gateway and the simulator run on one machine and share its
  CPU, memory and loopback stack. All values contain that bias.
- **Closed model.** Latency is measured from the actual send. Coordinated omission is not corrected.
- **Snapshot deltas.** See the section "Gateway and simulator deltas".
- **Median and range across repetitions.** The median of the per-run values of one mode in one cell (the
  mean of the two middle values for an even number) and their minimum and maximum. Never a percentile of
  pooled data.
- **ABBA position.** `1st` when the run came first in its pair, otherwise `2nd`. It is derived from
  `orderLabel` and the recorded mode order.
- **Rounding.** All computation is exact integer or decimal arithmetic. Times are rounded from nanoseconds
  to microseconds and shown in milliseconds with three decimals, rates with two decimals, shares in percent
  with two decimals, CPU load with three decimals, memory in GiB with one decimal (half-even rounding).
  Exception: in the comparison tables and sentences the values of a cell are shown with as many decimals as are
  needed to keep the facts the rule used visible (the two medians, the difference of the medians, ranges that do
  not overlap, the difference compared with the largest range); there times are not rounded to microseconds
  first. The rules always use the exact values.

## 9. Flag classification

Every flag of the runner's dictionary has a class. `exclude`: the run does not enter any comparison. `caution`: the run enters and is marked `*`. `info`: recorded only. A flag recorded for the whole set (`set` scope) as `exclude` excludes every run; as `caution` it appears only in the identification block. Every flag recorded in a warm-up phase counts as `caution` (warm-up anomaly) and never excludes. A flag that is not in the dictionary excludes the run (except in a warm-up phase, where it is a caution) and is listed as unknown. A run whose status is not `completed` is excluded.

| Flag or check | Class | Scope | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| `OUTCOME_INTERRUPTED_NONZERO` | exclude | run | drain timeout interrupted streams, the distributions are censored |
| `OUTCOME_<NAME>_NONZERO` | caution | run | errors are part of the observation, the shares are reported |
| `REJECTED_AT_OR_BELOW_LIMIT` | caution | run | unexpected rejection, the share is reported |
| `LOADGEN_EXIT_NONZERO` | exclude | run | the load generator did not finish properly |
| `LOADGEN_WAIT_EXCEEDED` | exclude | run | the load generator did not finish properly |
| `SUMMARY_MISSING` | caution | run | the JSONL is the result itself (ADR-0004), only the cross-check is lost |
| `JSONL_HEADER_UNEXPECTED` | exclude | run | the file is incomplete or the run did not end by duration |
| `JSONL_FOOTER_MISSING` | exclude | run | the file is incomplete or the run did not end by duration |
| `STOP_REASON_NOT_DURATION` | exclude | run | the file is incomplete or the run did not end by duration |
| `FOOTER_INTERRUPTED_NONZERO` | exclude | run | the file is incomplete or the run did not end by duration |
| `ACTIVE_STREAMS_NOT_ZERO_BEFORE` | exclude | run | the measurement started with leftover streams |
| `ACTIVE_STREAMS_NOT_ZERO_AFTER` | caution | run | state after the measurement, the data is complete |
| `QUEUE_DEPTH_NOT_ZERO_AFTER` | caution | run | state after the measurement, the data is complete |
| `REJECTED_REASON_SHUTDOWN_DELTA_NONZERO` | exclude | run | shutdown started during the measurement |
| `REJECTED_REASON_<R>_DELTA_NONZERO` | caution | run | behaviour of the system under test |
| `TIMEOUTS_DELTA_NONZERO` | caution | run | not expected without a fault, but it is behaviour of the system under test |
| `RETRIES_DELTA_NONZERO` | caution | run | not expected without a fault, but it is behaviour of the system under test |
| `RETRY_EXHAUSTED_DELTA_NONZERO` | caution | run | not expected without a fault, but it is behaviour of the system under test |
| `SIMULATOR_ACTIVE_GENERATIONS_NOT_ZERO_AFTER` | caution | run | additional observation, simulator deltas may be n/a |
| `SIMULATOR_REJECTED_DELTA_NONZERO` | caution | run | additional observation, simulator deltas may be n/a |
| `SIMULATOR_STATS_UNAVAILABLE` | caution | run | additional observation, simulator deltas may be n/a |
| `SIMULATOR_FAULTED_DELTA_NONZERO` | exclude | run | the pinned workload has no faults, the workload deviated from the protocol |
| `GATEWAY_EXITED` | exclude | run | the run data cannot be used |
| `SIMULATOR_EXITED` | exclude | run | the run data cannot be used |
| `CONNECTION_MODE_MISMATCH` | exclude | run | the run data cannot be used |
| `PORT_NOT_FREED` | caution | run | recorded after the measurement, the port check of the next run catches it |
| `CPU_BUSY_BEFORE_RUN` | exclude | run | the runner's own marker (cpuBusyThreshold) saw background load before the measurement |
| `CPU_LOAD_UNAVAILABLE` | caution | run | the data is complete, diagnostic information is missing |
| `LOG_TRUNCATED` | caution | run | the data is complete, diagnostic information is missing |
| `LOG_WRITE_ERROR` | caution | run | the data is complete, diagnostic information is missing |
| `TIME_WAIT_UNAVAILABLE` | info | set and run | environment record |
| `OUTPUT_NOT_GITIGNORED` | info | set | environment record |
| `GIT_DIRTY` | caution | set | identification banner |
| `GIT_UNAVAILABLE` | caution | set | identification banner |
| `ARTIFACT_OLDER_THAN_HEAD` | caution | set | identification banner |
| `CHECKLIST_NOT_CONFIRMED` | caution | set | identification banner |

| `INTERRUPTED` | caution | set | identification banner; the interrupted run is excluded by its status |

## 10. Limits

The following list is quoted verbatim from section 2 of the [benchmark protocol](benchmark-protocol.md).
It applies to every result set of that protocol, including this one.

<!-- quoted-limits:begin -->
- Anything about a real LLM, a real network, TLS, several hosts or production hardware: everything is synthetic and
  runs on `127.0.0.1` on one machine.
- Absolute capacity. The load generator, the gateway and the simulator share the CPU, memory and loopback stack of
  one machine. That is a bias of the set-up that no flag removes.
- Latency under a fixed arrival rate. The load model is closed (a fixed number of workers, each opening the next
  stream when the previous one ended), so coordinated omission is not corrected.
- Differences smaller than the run-to-run variation of the machine. The protocol records several repetitions per
  cell; whether they suffice is a question for the analysis step.
- Causes. The raw data can show that two modes differ; it cannot show why.
<!-- quoted-limits:end -->

In addition: the numbers above are observations of one result set. They are not a prediction for another
machine, another run set or production. The time to first byte is the arrival of the response headers, the
time to first chunk has the resolution of buffer arrival, the closed model does not correct coordinated
omission, the reject pause adds think time to rejected-heavy runs, and everything ran on one machine.

## 11. How to regenerate

The report is generated; do not edit it. The result set itself is never modified and is not committed.
To regenerate it from an archived result set, extract the archive into a new, empty directory outside
the repository (the extracted directory is the one that contains `manifest.json`), build the tool and run
it:

```bash
tar -xzf bench-<run-id>.tar.gz -C <new-empty-directory>
./mvnw -B package -DskipTests
java -jar report/target/report-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --results <new-empty-directory>/<run-id> --check
java -jar report/target/report-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --results <new-empty-directory>/<run-id> --out docs --overwrite
```

The same input gives byte-identical output. Without a result set,
`java -jar report/target/report-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar --placeholder --out docs --overwrite` writes the
placeholder version of this file. The data files are written to `docs/benchmark/`.

Derived data: [runs.csv](benchmark/runs.csv), [cells.csv](benchmark/cells.csv),
[analysis.json](benchmark/analysis.json) and the charts listed with the comparisons. In the CSV files a
text cell that starts with an equals sign, a plus sign, a minus sign, an at sign, a tab, a carriage return
or a line feed is prefixed with a single quote (spreadsheet formula injection); numeric columns are written
as they are.
